faq.a: Yes. A desert is a place with very little rain or snow, and inland Antarctica gets only about 50 millimetres a year. That makes it the biggest desert on Earth.
asks: Why is Antarctica called a desert?

faq.q: What is the biggest hot desert?
faq.a: The Sahara in North Africa, about 9.2 million square kilometres. It stretches across 11 countries, including Egypt, Algeria and Mali.

faq.q: What makes a place a desert?
faq.a: Very little rain or snow, usually less than 250 millimetres in a year. Heat has nothing to do with it.

faq.q: Why does so little snow fall in Antarctica?
faq.a: Very cold air cannot hold much water vapour, which is water in the air as a gas. With little water in the air, very little snow can fall.

faq.q: What is the driest place on Earth?
faq.a: Parts of the Atacama Desert in Chile and the Dry Valleys of Antarctica are the driest places, with almost no rain or snow for years.

facts: A desert is usually defined as a place receiving less than 250 millimetres of precipitation a year.
The Antarctic Desert, about 14 million square kilometres, is the largest desert on Earth.
